Simulated crime events for an example city

Source: R/data.R
sim_events.Rd

A small simulated spatio-temporal point pattern, provided so that the package's examples and vignette can be run without a real crime dataset.

Usage

sim_events

Format

An sf::sf object with 375 rows and 3 columns:

id

Integer event identifier.

date

Event date, a Date, between 2021-01-01 and 2023-12-31.

geometry

POINT geometry in EPSG:32717 (UTM zone 17S, metres).

Source

Simulated by data-raw/make-example-data.R in the package's GitHub repository, https://github.com/HenriquesCadbyLab/spHawkes.

Details

These are not real crime records. The pattern is drawn from a branching process shaped like the model fit_semihawkes() estimates, so each fitted component has genuine structure to recover rather than noise:

spatial background

three Gaussian hotspots over a uniform floor

long-term trend

immigration rate rising across the three years

day of week

weekends elevated relative to weekdays

triggering

each event spawns Poisson(0.35) offspring, roughly 300 m and 5 days away

The generating values are recorded here because they are useful as targets when checking that the estimator recovers what it should: branching ratio A = 0.35, triggering length scale 300 m, triggering time scale 5 days. Of the 375 simulated events, 260 are background and 115 (30.7%) triggered.

See also

sim_region for the matching study-area boundary.

Examples

ev <- prepare_events(sim_events, sim_region, date_col = "date")
print(ev)
#> <semihawkes_events>
#>   Study period : 2021-01-03 to 2024-01-01 (TT = 1093.0 days)
#>   Events kept  : 375 / 375 input rows
#>   Dropped      : 0 outside region, 0 outside date range
#>   CRS          : EPSG:32717
